In Budapest, in cohesive soil, the foundation level must be at least 0.8 m deep because of frost.
Ice lenses cannot lift a foundation placed below the frost line. The rule applies to light outbuildings too.
Fill of unknown composition can be treated as a bearing stratum if it is thick enough.
Unknown fill is heterogeneous and compressible, and its thickness does not help. You have to found below it or treat it by ground improvement.
The bearing capacity factors increase linearly, in proportion to the angle of shearing resistance.
They increase steeply: from 30° to 35°, N<sub>q</sub> nearly doubles; from 20° to 35°, N<sub>γ</sub> increases more than tenfold.
In DA-2*, the actions are taken at their characteristic values and the partial factors are applied at the end.
That is why the eccentricity and the effective foundation dimensions are also determined from characteristic loads.
A rise in the groundwater level increases the bearing resistance of a shallow foundation.
It reduces it: below water the effective unit weight of the soil drops to about half, so the weight-dependent terms of the bearing resistance formula decrease too.
For undrained bearing resistance we work in total stresses.
Under rapid loading, the pore water in a saturated cohesive soil cannot drain away, so we use the undrained shear strength and total stresses.
If the resultant of the loads falls outside the middle third of the base (e > B/6), no pressure is transmitted under part of the base.
Part of the base “lifts off”. The effective foundation dimension is then considerably smaller than the actual one.
In a sliding check, the variable load is also included in the stabilising vertical force.
Only the permanent load counts: the variable load may be absent exactly when the horizontal force acts.
Under the Hungarian National Annex, overall stability is verified with DA-3.
In DA-3 the shear strength parameters are divided by partial factors.
Uplift of a watertight basement is a threat only once the building is complete.
It is most dangerous during construction: the structure is still light while the water pressure is already at full value. That is why dewatering has to be maintained until the weight is sufficient.
The influence depth is where the additional stress drops to 20 % of the effective overburden stress.
Below the influence depth the compression of the soil is negligible.
Uniform settlement is always more dangerous than differential settlement.
The other way round: the structure is cracked by differential settlement and angular distortion. A building that settles uniformly can tolerate even several centimetres without damage.
A diagonal crack rises towards the part of the wall that has settled more.
From this crack pattern you can work backwards to where the foundation settled more.
Grouting permanently stops the movements caused by shrinking and swelling clay.
The movement is caused by the seasonal change in water content. The only lasting solution is to take the foundation below the desiccation zone.
On loess, water soaking in from a burst pipe can cause sudden, large settlement.
Collapsible loess is strong when dry, but when soaked its loose skeleton collapses.
The compression of peat is complete shortly after loading.
Peat creeps for years, so its settlement is often much larger than the value measured in the first months.
Frost lifts the foundation of a light, unheated outbuilding less than that of a heavy house.
Quite the opposite: ice lenses lift a light building more easily, and the ground beneath it freezes to the full depth.
Vibration from driven piling can densify the sand beneath neighbouring buildings and cause settlement.
That is why bored or vibration-free techniques are chosen next to existing buildings.
When a CFA pile is drilled, the borehole wall is supported by casing or slurry.
The soil between the flights of the auger supports the wall, and the concrete is pumped in from the bottom as the auger is withdrawn.
An end-bearing pile transmits most of its load through the base.
For an end-bearing pile, the base resistance is at least two thirds of the total resistance; for a friction pile, the shaft resistance is.
If the bearing stratum is deep, a deep foundation can be more economical than a shallow one.
The pile carries the load through the weak layers into the bearing stratum.
A soldier pile wall (Berlin wall) is a watertight form of excavation support.
Water seeps through the gaps between the lagging boards, so it can only be used above the water table or together with dewatering.
A diaphragm wall can be part of the permanent basement wall.
A reinforced concrete diaphragm wall is watertight and stiff, so after supporting the excavation it remains part of the basement structure.
The fixed length of a ground anchor must lie within the potential slip surface.
It must lie beyond the slip surface, outside the sliding wedge, in a competent stratum – otherwise the anchor moves together with the soil.
For a pad footing, the investigation depth is 2 m regardless of the footing width.
Below foundation level the investigation must reach at least three times the footing width, and at least 6 m.
